plan: [ This is a sealed-bid, second-price (Vickrey) auction: if I win, I pay the highest competing bid. The dominant strategy is to bid my true value, regardless of others’ strategies, because overbidding risks winning at a price above my value and underbidding risks losing when I would have profited. There’s only 1 round, so no dynamic learning applies. To maximize expected profit while avoiding overpayment risk, I will bid exactly my value. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction: if I win, I pay the highest competing bid. With independent private values and no informative history (round 1 of 1), bidding my true value is a weakly dominant strategy that maximizes expected profit. Any higher bid risks overpaying if others shade up; any lower bid risks losing when winning would be profitable. Therefore, bid exactly my value $8. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction: winner pays the highest competing bid. With independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid truthfully. Overbidding risks negative profit if price exceeds value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. There’s only 1 round, so no learning advantage this time. My value is 44, bids allowed in 0.1 increments, so bid exactly 44 to maximize expected profit. If I win, profit = 44 − (highest rival bid). ]
